full_judgment:
3. Mr. Ahmed Hussain, the learned Advocate, appearing for the official liquidator respondent has submitted two preliminary objections as to the maintainability of this appeal. First objection is that the appeal is barred by limitation and the second objection is that the appeal is not maintainable in view of the provision of section 72 of the Banking Companies Act, 1962. 

 4. Mr. S. S. Halder, the learned Advocate appearing in support of the appeal has with regard to the first preliminary objection contended that the appeal was not barred by limitation because it has been filed within 20 days from the date of drawing up of the order. The order was drawn up on 19.12.73 and the Memo of Appeal was presented before this Court on 8.1.74 that is within twenty days. Mr. Ahmed Hussain, the learned Advocate has from drawn up order as is found in the paper book, submitted that it was drawn up on 22.3.73. We have, however, checked up the records of this court and have found that the judgment was delivered on the 22nd March, 1973 and the requisite for drawing up of the order, was put in by the official liquidator, on the very same date and the drawn up order was signed by the Registrar of this Court on 19.12.73. This being the position we find no substance in the first preliminary object ion raised by the learned Advocate for the official liquidator.
